summary: myidsan gains an in-app config editor over a safe subset of config.json — localAuth, sso, security, storage, logging — the last of the four apps to get one, ported and adapted from myseliasan's settings feature. GET /api/settings, GET/PUT /api/settings/{section}, POST /api/settings/{section}/reset, and POST /api/settings/cache/test are superadmin-only (enforced as route-group middleware, matching audit/backup/mfa-admin), and a save writes the changed leaves back into config.json (every other block preserved byte-for-byte) and reports needsRestart. The security section is the standout: it surfaces the lockout, password-policy, and MFA-policy blocks through their resolved Effective*() values, so an operator can finally see what those absent-from-config blocks resolve to instead of a misleading zero/off reading, with validation floors (maxAttempts >= 2 once lockout is on, minLength >= 8, a known mfa.policy value); mfa.requiredRoleIds is shown read-only because the save path never writes it. audit.retention is deliberately not exposed, and neither are kerberos, login.oidc[]/social providers, or the new webauthn block. Unlike myseliasan's port, there is no server-side file-browse endpoint, since myidsan is the identity provider and the highest-value target in the suite; the sso section only exposes the provider (issuing) side of the shared config block, and authCodeTtlSeconds is capped at 600 seconds. Saves/resets are recorded in the audit trail (section and actor only, never values). The React Settings page has now shipped as a tabbed editor (one tab per section plus a System tab) of grouped cards with per-field (i) info tips, masked secrets (blank keeps the stored value), a dirty-gated Save, per-section Restore-defaults, and a persistent "restart required" banner. A companion POST /api/system/restart endpoint (superadmin-gated middleware, never delegable through the permission matrix) relaunches the process so that banner's Restart button actually does something — without it the page would name a required action it had no way to perform. Verified live: all 6 tabs render, save/validate/reset exercised against a running server, the audit entry confirmed, zero console errors.
compatibility: Adds a new superadmin-only API surface (settings + system/restart) and two new seeded endpoint rows + one System-group nav item ("Settings"); no existing behavior changes for any current install, and no new config keys are required — every editable section already has defaults. Saving through the API still requires a process restart to take effect, exactly like every other infra-block edit on this app; the new /api/system/restart endpoint is what performs that restart from inside the product instead of requiring shell/service-manager access. Nil-database construction is still supported (disables only the reset-to-defaults snapshot), so no migration or first-boot cost is imposed on existing databases.
